title: A triage report
description:
Turn the facts gathered in triage (lessons 1.05 and 6.01) into the warnings an analyst writes at the top of their notes:

```cpp
struct SectionFacts { std::string name; double entropy; bool write; bool execute; };
struct Facts { std::vector<SectionFacts> sections; int importCount; std::string entrySection; bool hasDebugInfo; };

std::vector<std::string> triageFlags(const Facts& f);
```

Return the flags that apply, in exactly this order:

| Flag | When |
|---|---|
| `"no imports"` | `importCount` is 0 |
| `"few imports"` | `importCount` is 1 to 9 |
| `"high entropy: NAME"` | a section's entropy is above 7.2 (one flag per such section, in section order) |
| `"writable code: NAME"` | a section is both writable and executable (one per section) |
| `"entry outside .text"` | `entrySection` is not `.text` |
| `"probably packed"` | at least one high-entropy section **and** fewer than 10 imports |
| `"symbols may be available"` | `hasDebugInfo` is true |
hints: Go through the rules in the order of the table, appending as you go; remember whether you saw any high-entropy section for the "probably packed" rule.
